COMPONENT_GRAPH.architecture_style: single-process Go edge runtime with immutable serving generations, serialized reconciliation, shared lifecycle-safe runtime objects, explicit operator/data planes, and durable recovery

identity_contract.endpoint_identity: pool id + canonical network endpoint + transport compatibility key; textual aliases normalize before duplicate detection
identity_contract.endpoint_incarnation: continuous membership may reuse compatible runtime state; accepted removal followed by later re-add creates a new incarnation
identity_contract.pool_identity: stable pool id plus compatibility fingerprint for selection/affinity semantics
identity_contract.route_identity: stable route id plus semantic digest independent of declaration ordering
identity_contract.source_fence: source identity + monotonic revision + canonical content digest; lower revision is stale, same revision+digest is idempotent, same revision+different digest is conflict

DATA_VOLUME_PLAN.anti_padding: Variation must affect routing/reconciliation behavior; do not duplicate routes/endpoints merely to inflate size.
DATA_VOLUME_PLAN.classification: configuration/runtime-state backed edge service, not a primary business-record database; the 10k–20k primary-business-record default is not naturally applicable
DATA_VOLUME_PLAN.plan: Use deterministic materially varied production-scale route/pool/endpoint configuration and multiple independent source snapshots/regions/revisions sufficient to exercise reconciliation, identity, health, selection, drain and recovery interactions; generated configuration volume does not count as authored-code scale.

ENTRYPOINTS: `edge-router-runtime serve` -> bootstrap/recovery -> public data-plane listener + separate operator listener -> provider/watch ingestion -> generation reconciliation.
`edge-router-runtime validate` -> parse/normalize/semantic validation/compile checks without publishing or mutating serving/recovery state.
Operator configuration/discovery apply endpoints -> bounded ingress -> source fencing -> validate/compile -> reconcile -> durable checkpoint/publication -> explicit accepted/rejected response.
Public HTTP request -> acquire one RuntimeSnapshot lease -> route match -> pool/affinity/health eligibility -> retry/failover selection -> endpoint-scoped transport -> telemetry -> release lease.

Startup recovery -> verify CURRENT/checksum/schema -> fall back to previous complete body/bootstrap when needed -> normalize/revalidate/recompile -> install source fences -> publish one recovered generation before readiness.
Shutdown/drain -> stop new acceptance -> retain leased snapshots/in-flight endpoint incarnations within policy -> retire transports/state -> persist bounded telemetry/recovery state.
PRODUCTION_CHARACTERISTICS: Real public data plane and separate operator plane with explicit startup/readiness/shutdown ownership.
Single-writer control-plane reconciliation with concurrent immutable readers, stale/conflicting generation fencing and last-known-good preservation.
Differentiated route compilation, runtime-state ownership, selection, health, transport, drain, checkpoint and telemetry responsibilities rather than copied modules.
State reuse based on stable semantic identities and membership incarnations, preserving continuity without reviving retired objects.
Crash-safe durable generation bodies and recoverable authority with checksum/schema validation and previous-generation fallback.
Health-aware weighted/sticky/retry/failover routing with explicit all-ineligible behavior and bounded retry semantics.
Lifecycle-aware connection draining, long-lived request leases, final transport cleanup, bounded affinity and telemetry garbage collection.
Validation/error handling across malformed/cross-object configuration, duplicate canonical endpoints, invalid policy bounds, stale/conflicting revisions and corrupt recovery state.
Normal operator/configuration workflows reach the same production implementation; no dead scale or repair-only entrypoints.

SCALE_FIT.anti_padding: No primary business-record corpus, copied module skeleton, decorative resource count, or split/renamed test behavior is required to meet strict scale.
SCALE_FIT.behavioral_breadth: Generation fencing, atomicity, state reuse, health/selection, drain/retirement, checkpoint/recovery and bounded telemetry create 20–30 coupled manifestations and an organic 25–30 distinct F2P surface plus preservation cases.
SCALE_FIT.edge_failure_breadth: Includes stale/conflicting revisions, invalid candidates, duplicate identities, concurrent readers/writers, all-backends-ineligible, retry exclusion, active traffic during removal, rapid re-add, drain deadlines, corruption/partial recovery and telemetry reclamation.
SCALE_FIT.substantive_runtime_plan: The clean architecture naturally spans bootstrap/config/compiler/reconcile/runtime/router/selection/upstream/health/drain/checkpoint/telemetry/admin modules with materially different responsibilities and normal reachability; it supports well above the 3,000 substantive solver-visible LOC floor without duplication.

STATE_MODEL.affinity: bounded expiring hint keyed to canonical endpoint identity/incarnation; lookup never bypasses current generation, health or lifecycle eligibility
STATE_MODEL.checkpoint: immutable checksummed generation bodies plus atomically replaced CURRENT authority and previous complete fallback; recovered desired state is revalidated/recompiled rather than deserializing partial runtime objects
STATE_MODEL.endpoint_membership: ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> RETIRED; new assignment requires membership in the leased snapshot, same incarnation, ACTIVE lifecycle and health eligibility
STATE_MODEL.generation: immutable RuntimeSnapshot containing compiled route graph, pool membership views, normalized desired state, source fences, semantic/generation digest and references to runtime-owned objects
STATE_MODEL.health: UNKNOWN | HEALTHY | UNHEALTHY, mutable independently of configuration publication; active/passive signals attach to endpoint incarnation
STATE_MODEL.retirement: snapshot, endpoint, transport, affinity and telemetry ownership is reclaimed only after generation/reference/in-flight policy permits final retirement
STATE_MODEL.retry: request-local canonical endpoint exclusion prevents reselecting a failed alias/incarnation; exhausted primary+failover returns deterministic unavailable
STATE_MODEL.source_fencing: per-source accepted revision/digest installed atomically with accepted generation semantics; candidates are rechecked after compile before publication

UNRESOLVED_RISKS: Drain-deadline behavior for very long-lived upgraded/streaming requests must be explicit in the later solver-visible requirement contract so safe retirement is gradable without implementation prescription.
Checkpoint ordering must keep recoverable authority coherent with publication semantics; later defect design may target behavioral surfaces but may not change this clean invariant.
Provider/source merge precedence must remain deterministic and documented if multiple regional/discovery sources define overlapping objects.
